div.div:
Blocks when every core is busy. Above
~500k IOPS this, and not the device,
is the constraint.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 261px; margin-left: 2px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#666666, #959595); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
A read hit never becomes a request.
A dirty page cannot be dropped —
its frame is only reusable once the
bytes have reached the device.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 349px; margin-left: 2px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#666666, #959595); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Sequential access is subsidised;
scattered access is taxed. A miss the
kernel does not recognize seeds four
pages where one was asked for, and a
scattered stream uses none of them.
POSIX_FADV_RANDOM is the remedy.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 489px; margin-left: 2px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#666666, #959595); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
A buffered write does not wait on the
device — it waits on the throttle. The
sustained rate is the drain rate either
way; memory only decides how long the
illusion lasts.
Which of the two exits a page takes is
decided by access order, not by memory.
A scattered reader claims the frames
holding output pages the flusher has
not written yet, so its writeback
fragments even when its writes are
perfectly ordered.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 535px; margin-left: 552px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#666666, #959595); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Reordering only pays against a device that does not
reorder. The lock does not care: at 100% busy it caps
mq-deadline at 569k and bfq at 315k IOPS, and adding
cores does not lift it.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 121px; margin-left: 1212px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#666666, #959595); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Full ⇒ the issuer waits. This is queue saturation —
and a buffered write is exempt, because it issues
no command to be queued.

div.div:

every flash curve.

display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#666666, #959595); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
A busy die blocks the request that lands
on it, however idle the rest of the device is.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 403px; margin-left: 1212px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#666666, #959595); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Consumes no bandwidth. On a disk under
scattered 4 KiB reads this is 99% of busy time.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 591px; margin-left: 1212px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#666666, #959595); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
A write is acknowledged once it is buffered,
while its dies keep programming.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 685px; margin-left: 1212px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#333333, #c1c1c1); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Whichever ceiling is lowest
host cores · scheduler lock · queue depth
controller rate · link and memory bandwidth
die availability · the writeback throttle

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 812px; margin-left: 252px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#666666, #959595); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-style: italic; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
The run is not over when the last write returns. Dirty pages are drained to the device before the clock stops —
without that barrier a buffered rewrite reports the time it took to fill memory.
